Throughout this page, assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]): the
analytic and cohomological suppliers invoked by the results below assume full
AC, and each item records its exact use. The definitional content below uses no
choice.

**(1) Compact Kähler manifolds.** Let $n\ge1$. A **Kähler manifold** is a complex
manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with complex structure
$J$ and a **Hermitian metric** $g$ — a Riemannian metric
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$ — whose **real fundamental form**
$\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ is

- a smooth real 2-form, the section of $\Lambda^2T^*X$ obtained by alternating
  $g(J\cdot,\cdot)$;
- **positive**: $\omega(v,Jv)=g(Jv,Jv)>0$ for every nonzero tangent vector $v$;
- **closed**: $d\omega=0$.

The manifold is **compact Kähler** when the topological space $X$ is compact.

**Orientation.** For a complex basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ of a tangent space $T_xX$,
the ordered real basis $(v_1,Jv_1,\dots,v_n,Jv_n)$ is declared **positive**. This
is well defined: two complex bases differ by a complex-linear automorphism, whose
real determinant is the square of the modulus of its complex determinant and so
is positive, and the local orientations therefore glue along holomorphic charts
to a global orientation of $X$. Let $v_1,\dots,v_n$ be a $g$-orthonormal complex
frame, so $g(v_j,v_k)=\delta_{jk}$ and $g(v_j,Jv_k)=0$, and let $e_j=g(v_j,\cdot)$ and
$f_j=g(Jv_j,\cdot)$ be the metric-dual covectors. Then
$(e_1,f_1,\dots,e_n,f_n)$ is a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe,
$f_j=-Je_j$ for the pullback action $(J\alpha)(v)=\alpha(Jv)$ of $J$ on
covectors, and

$$\omega=\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\wedge f_j .$$

The **oriented volume form** is the top form

$$dV:=\frac{\omega^n}{n!}=e_1\wedge f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n\wedge f_n ,$$

which evaluates to $1$ on each positively oriented $g$-orthonormal frame.

**Complex dimension zero.** For $n=0$ a complex manifold is a discrete space and
compactness makes it a finite set of points with its unique complex structure;
there are no tangent vectors and no forms of positive degree, $\omega=0$, and the
operators $L,\Lambda,\partial,\bar\partial,d,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ and
all Laplacians introduced below are zero. The Hodge star is the identity on
degree zero, and $dV$ is the counting measure.

**(2) Complex-valued forms and Kähler operators.** Let $X$ be compact Kähler.
Write $\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ for the complex-valued smooth $k$-forms, the
complex-linear extension of the real forms of
[[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]; the Hodge star $*$ of
[[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] extends complex-linearly, and for
$\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ the **integral inner product**

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\int_X\alpha\wedge*\bar\beta$$

is complex-linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second; the
integral is that of
[[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]] and
the integrand is $\lvert\alpha\rvert^2\,dV$ when $\beta=\alpha$, so the pairing
is a positive definite Hermitian form. In holomorphic charts

$$\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(X),\qquad d=\partial+\bar\partial ,$$

with $\partial$ and $\bar\partial$ of bidegree $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$
([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]); the decomposition is independent
of the holomorphic chart because holomorphic chart changes preserve bidegree.

Put $L=\omega\wedge$, so that $L:\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)\to\Omega^{k+2}(X;\mathbb C)$,
and let $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ be the formal adjoints of
$L,\partial,\bar\partial,d$ with respect to $\langle\,,\rangle$; existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]], applied
to the bundle of complex-valued forms with the metric of
[[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]
and the density $dV$. The **Laplacians** are

$$\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d,\qquad \Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial,\qquad \Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial ,$$

and $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

**(3) Rational pure Hodge structures.** Let $k\in\mathbb Z$. A **rational pure
Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space
$V$ together with a direct-sum decomposition by $\mathbb C$-subspaces

$$V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q},\qquad \overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p},$$

where conjugation is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear involution
$v\otimes\lambda\mapsto v\otimes\bar\lambda$. The sum is finite because
$V_{\mathbb C}$ is finite dimensional, and it is direct by definition. The **Weil
operator** $C$ is the $\mathbb C$-linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathbb C}$ acting
as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$; the conjugation symmetry makes $C$ commute with
conjugation, so $C$ is the complexification of a real-linear endomorphism
of $V_{\mathbb R}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb R$. It need not preserve $V$.

A **polarization** of such a Hodge structure is a nondegenerate $\mathbb Q$-bilinear
form $Q:V\times V\to\mathbb Q$, extended $\mathbb C$-bilinearly to $V_{\mathbb C}$,
such that

- $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$ for all $x,y$;
- $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$;
- $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ is a positive definite Hermitian form on $V_{\mathbb C}$.

A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace
$U\subseteq V$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$.
The **Tate shift** $V(-r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, keeps the underlying $\mathbb Q$-vector
space, the Weil operator and $Q$ as they are and moves the bidegrees to
$(p+r,q+r)$, so that the weight becomes $k+2r$; equivalently, $(V(-r))^{p,q}=V^{p-r,q-r}$.

Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary of
dimension $n\ge2$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let $\mu$ be a smooth positive
density on $M$ ([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), and let $E\to M$ be
a finite-rank smooth vector bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]]) over
$\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ carrying a smooth bundle metric
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ ([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]), Euclidean in the
real case and Hermitian, linear in the first variable, in the complex case; in
the complex case the fibres are complex vector spaces through a smooth complex
structure on $E$
([[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]). Write $\Gamma(E)$
for the smooth sections ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).

A $\mathbb K$-linear map $P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(E)$ is a **linear differential
operator of order at most two** on $E$ when, on every chart domain $\Omega$ of
$M$ with coordinates $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$ and in every local frame of $E$ over
$\Omega$ in which a section is written $s\leftrightarrow u=(u^1,\ldots,u^r)$
and its image as $Ps\leftrightarrow((Ps)_1,\ldots,(Ps)_r)$,
$$(Ps)_\lambda=-\sum_{i,j=1}^na^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_i\partial_ju^\mu(x)+\sum_{j=1}^nb^j_{\lambda\mu}(x)\,\partial_ju^\mu(x)+c_{\lambda\mu}(x)u^\mu(x),\qquad1\le\lambda\le r,$$
with smooth coefficient functions on $\Omega$ and summation over the repeated
index $\mu$ (and over $i,j$). Such an operator is **Laplace type** when in
addition, in every such chart and frame, its second-order coefficients are
scalar multiples of the identity, $a^{ij}_{\lambda\mu}=a^{ij}\delta_{\lambda\mu}$,
with $a^{ij}$ smooth real functions for which the matrix $(a^{ij}(x))$ is
symmetric and positive definite at every $x\in\Omega$. Its **principal symbol**
is the endomorphism-valued quadratic function
$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a^{ij}(x)\xi_i\xi_j\,\mathrm{id}_{E_x}$ for
$\xi\in T_x^*M$. Its scalar principal form $a$ is a smooth section of
$\mathrm{Sym}^2TM$ ([[def-smooth-tensor-field]]), since it acts on two
covectors, and $a_x(\xi,\xi)>0$ for $\xi\ne0$. For positive-rank $E$ the
symbol determines $a$ uniquely. On the zero-rank bundle the operator and its
symbol are zero; a supplied smooth positive-definite form $a$ is part of the
Laplace-type data in this degenerate case.

For the density-integral convention assume Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). $P$ is **formally symmetric** for
$(\mu,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ when
$$\int_M\langle Ps,t\rangle\,d\mu=\int_M\langle s,Pt\rangle\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $s,t\in\Gamma_c(E)$
([[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]).

**Well-definedness.** The definition is local. On a fixed chart and frame the
displayed assignment is a $\mathbb K$-linear map on components with smooth
coefficients, and the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]])
computes the transition to another chart and frame on the overlap: the
second-order coefficients transform by the symmetric tensor rule
$a'^{kl}=a^{ij}\frac{\partial x'^k}{\partial x^i}\frac{\partial x'^l}{\partial x^j}$
together with conjugation by the frame-change matrix, while the terms produced
by the second derivatives of the coordinate change are absorbed into the
first-order coefficients. Hence a single operator that admits a local
expression on one cover admits a local expression on every chart and frame, and
the two hypotheses placed on the leading coefficient are invariant: scalar-ness
is preserved by frame conjugation and by the coordinate rule for a field of
symmetric matrices, and symmetric positive definiteness is preserved by both.
For positive rank the scalar principal form, and in every rank the principal
symbol, are therefore independent of the chart and frame, since two
local expressions of the same operator differ by an operator of order at most
one; the symbol is smooth in $(x,\xi)$ because the $a^{ij}$ are smooth, and
the scalar principal form is positive on nonzero covectors exactly when
$(a^{ij})$ is positive definite.
Formal symmetry is an identity between integrals of compactly supported smooth
sections and therefore depends only on the operator, the density and the
metric.

Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary,
$\mu$ a smooth positive density on $M$, and $E,F\to M$ finite-rank smooth vector
bundles over $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ with smooth bundle metrics,
Hermitian (first-variable-linear) in the complex case, with the conventions of
[[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]. Let
$P:\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(F)$ be a linear differential operator of order at most two
(the target-$F$ version of the local description in
[[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]]).

Then there is a unique linear differential operator $P^\star:\Gamma(F)\to\Gamma(E)$
of order at most two such that
$$\int_M\langle Pu,v\rangle_F\,d\mu=\int_M\langle u,P^\star v\rangle_E\,d\mu$$
for all compactly supported smooth sections $u\in\Gamma_c(E)$ and
$v\in\Gamma_c(F)$; it is the **formal adjoint** of $P$. It is given locally as
follows: in a chart with coordinates $x$, with density coefficient $\gamma>0$
defined by $\mu=\gamma\,|dx^1\cdots dx^n|$
([[def-density-bundle-and-smooth-density]]), with frames of $E$ and $F$
orthonormal for the metrics (equivalently unitary in the complex case; such
frames exist locally by applying Gram–Schmidt to any local frame,
[[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]), and with local coefficients
$Pu=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}a_\alpha D^\alpha u$,
$$P^\star v=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\gamma^{-1}D^\alpha\bigl(\gamma\,a_\alpha^*v\bigr),$$
where $a_\alpha^*$ is the fibre adjoint. Consequently:
1. if the leading coefficients of $P$ of order $\delta\in\{0,1,2\}$ are the
   matrices $a_\alpha$, $|\alpha|=\delta$, then those of $P^\star$ are
   $(-1)^\delta a_\alpha^*$, computed in the same orthonormal frames; in
   particular the formal adjoint of a Laplace-type operator is again Laplace
   type and its principal symbol is unchanged,
   $\sigma_2(P^\star)=\sigma_2(P)$;
2. $(P^\star)^\star=P$;
3. if $E=F$, then $P$ is formally symmetric in the sense of
   [[def-second-order-laplace-type-operators-on-vector-bundles]] exactly when
   $P=P^\star$.

The real **de Rham cohomology** is $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^k(M)/B^k(M)$, with $Z^k,B^k$ as in [[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]].

This is [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]] in real vector spaces. Only a closed form $\omega$ represents a class $[\omega]$. For closed forms $\omega,\omega\prime$, equality $[\omega]=[\omega\prime]$ means precisely $\omega\prime-\omega=d\eta$ for some $(k-1)$-form $\eta$. Addition and real scalar multiplication are induced by those of forms. All groups on the empty manifold are zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with the
conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]].
Then the formal adjoints satisfy

$$[\Lambda,\partial]=i\bar\partial^*,\qquad [\Lambda,\bar\partial]=-i\partial^*,\qquad [\bar\partial^*,L]=i\partial,\qquad [\partial^*,L]=-i\bar\partial .$$

One has $\Delta_d=2\Delta_\partial=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$, the mixed anticommutators
$\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\partial$ and
$\bar\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\bar\partial$ vanish, and $\Delta_d$ commutes
with $L,\Lambda,\partial,\bar\partial,*$, and preserves each bidegree
$\Omega^{p,q}(X)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$. There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

Assume AC. For a compact smooth manifold $X$, the natural coefficient maps
induce isomorphisms $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}F\cong H^k(X;F)$ for
every characteristic-zero field $F$, finite-dimensional in each degree. For
$F=\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ these identify singular cohomology with the real or
complex de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps
between such manifolds. No ordered-field or positivity structure is asserted
for a general $F$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, integration on smooth simplices followed by the inverse of restriction from continuous to smooth singular cohomology gives a natural isomorphism of unital graded real algebras
$$J_M:H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*_{\mathrm{sing}}(M;\mathbb R).$$
The source product is wedge of form classes, the target product is the front/back singular cup product, and both stars denote direct sums of the homogeneous groups. Naturality is for smooth maps. No compactness assumption is imposed.

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth, and let $\omega\in\Omega^k(N)$. The **pullback**
$F^*\omega$ is the pullback of $\omega$ viewed as an alternating covariant
$k$-tensor field:

$$ (F^*\omega)_p(v_1,\ldots,v_k)=\omega_{F(p)}(dF_pv_1,\ldots,dF_pv_k). $$

For a smooth map $F:M\to N$, pullback sends smooth differential forms on $N$ to
smooth differential forms on $M$, is functorial, and satisfies

$$ F^*(\alpha\wedge\beta)=F^*\alpha\wedge F^*\beta. $$

Let $F:M\to N$ be smooth and let $\omega$ be a differential form on $N$.
If $d\omega=0$, then $d(F^*\omega)=0$; if $\omega=d\eta$ for a differential
form $\eta$ on $N$, then $F^*\omega=d(F^*\eta)$.

Let $m\ge1$. A **chart** on a topological space $X$ is a homeomorphism
$\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)$ from an open set $U\subseteq X$ onto an open subset of
$\mathbb C^m$ with its usual topology ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]);
two charts $\varphi,\psi$ are **holomorphically compatible** when the
transition maps $\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi\circ\psi^{-1}$ are
holomorphic on the open sets where they are defined
([[def-holomorphic-function-in-several-complex-variables]]). A **holomorphic
atlas** is a family of pairwise compatible charts whose domains cover $X$. A
**complex manifold of dimension $m$** is a nonempty Hausdorff
([[def-hausdorff-space]]) second-countable ([[def-second-countable-space]])
topological space carrying a holomorphic atlas; the same maximal-atlas argument
as for [[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]] applies verbatim with
$\mathbb C^m$ in place of $\mathbb C$: the union of a holomorphic atlas with all
charts compatible with it is again a holomorphic atlas, so one passes to the
unique maximal atlas and calls its members holomorphic charts. Each chart is a
homeomorphism onto an open subset of $\mathbb C^m\cong\mathbb R^{2m}$, so $X$ is
a topological manifold without boundary of real dimension $2m$
([[def-topological-manifold-without-boundary]]), and for connected $X$ the case
$m=1$ recovers Riemann surfaces ([[def-riemann-surface-and-holomorphic-atlas]]).

A **holomorphic map** $f:X\to Y$ between complex manifolds is a continuous map
whose expression in every pair of holomorphic charts is holomorphic
([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]]); equivalently, for every open
$V\subseteq Y$ and every holomorphic function $h$ on $V$, the function
$h\circ f$ is holomorphic on $f^{-1}(V)$. The forward implication is the
holomorphic chain rule; conversely apply this condition to the coordinate
functions of a chart on $Y$.

**Induced smooth structure and complex structure.** Holomorphic functions on
open subsets of $\mathbb C^m$ are smooth
([[cor-holomorphic-functions-in-several-variables-are-smooth]]), so every
holomorphic atlas is a smooth atlas ([[def-smooth-atlas]]) and $X$ is a smooth
manifold of real dimension $2m$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) whose smooth charts
include the holomorphic ones. In holomorphic coordinates
$z_k=x_k+iy_k$ the **complex structure** is the endomorphism field $J$ of the
tangent bundle determined by $J\partial_{x_k}=\partial_{y_k}$ and
$J\partial_{y_k}=-\partial_{x_k}$; it satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$ and is
independent of the holomorphic chart, because a holomorphic transition map has
complex-linear differential ([[def-holomorphic-map-and-complex-jacobian]],
[[thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables]]) and complex-linear
maps intertwine the two coordinate definitions of multiplication by $i$. A
**Hermitian metric** on $X$ is a Riemannian metric $g$
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$; its Riemannian volume density
is written $\mu_g$ ([[def-riemannian-volume-density]]). The complex structure
makes each tangent space a complex vector space, so the tangent bundle is a
smooth complex vector bundle in the sense of
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]].

**Holomorphic vector bundles and Hermitian bundle metrics.** A **holomorphic
vector bundle of rank $r$** on $X$ is a smooth complex vector bundle
$\pi:E\to X$ of rank $r$
([[def-smooth-vector-bundle-rank-fibre-and-trivial-bundle]],
[[def-complex-linear-and-compatible-bundle-connections]]) together with an open
cover $(V_\alpha)$ of $X$ and smooth local trivializations
$\theta_\alpha:E|_{V_\alpha}\to V_\alpha\times\mathbb C^r$ whose transition
matrices $g_{\alpha\beta}:V_\alpha\cap V_\beta\to\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb C)$,
defined by $\theta_\alpha\theta_\beta^{-1}(p,v)=(p,g_{\alpha\beta}(p)v)$, are
holomorphic. A **holomorphic frame** over an open set $V$ is a smooth
complex-linear trivialization whose transition matrices with the supplied
trivializations are holomorphic on every overlap. Changing holomorphic frame multiplies a local section by a
holomorphic matrix, hence a smooth local section is **holomorphic** exactly when
its representatives in holomorphic frames are holomorphic functions. A
**Hermitian metric** $h$ on $E$ is a smooth bundle metric
([[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]) whose fibre pairings are positive definite
Hermitian forms, linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the
second; the condition is frame-independent because the gauge freedom is
conjugation by a pointwise invertible matrix. Smooth sections are
$\Gamma(E)$ ([[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]).

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $P=\prod_{j=1}^n D_j$ and
$P'=\prod_{j=1}^n D'_j$ be finite open coordinate polydiscs such that each
closed coordinate disc $\overline{D'_j}$ is a compact subset of $D_j$. Let
$0\le p\le n$ and $1\le q\le n$, and let $\eta\in\Omega^{p,q}(P)$ be a
smooth form with $\bar\partial\eta=0$. Then there is a smooth
$\psi\in\Omega^{p,q-1}(P')$ such that
$$\bar\partial\psi=\eta|_{P'}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a topological space $X$, let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]), and let $I$ be the supplied
functorial injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ of
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every abelian
sheaf $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]).

For every $q\ge0$ and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ define the
**$q$-th sheaf cohomology group of $\mathcal F$** to be the right derived
object of $\Gamma(X,-)$ relative to $I$:
$$H^q(X,\mathcal F):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr),$$
the cohomology object of the complex
$\Gamma(X,I^0(\mathcal F))\to\Gamma(X,I^1(\mathcal F))\to\cdots$ of abelian
groups obtained from the deleted resolution
([[def-deleted-resolution]], [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]).
We also set $H^q(X,\mathcal F):=0$ for $q<0$.

Because $I$ is a fixed supplied datum, the group $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a
specific group for each pair $(X,\mathcal F)$, and for a morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves we write
$H^q(X,\varphi):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map; it is the map on
cohomology induced by $\Gamma(X,-)$ applied to the cochain maps supplied with
the datum, and it is additive in $\varphi$.

If $J$ is another supplied injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ then
$R_I^q\Gamma(X,-)$ and $R_J^q\Gamma(X,-)$ are naturally isomorphic, so the
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ computed from $J$ agree with the ones above up to a
canonical natural isomorphism; the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that
comparison follows from AC
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]],
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum used, up to this
canonical isomorphism, and we call $q$ the **cohomological degree**.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), let
$\mathcal A=\mathcal C_M^\infty$ be its sheaf of real-valued smooth functions,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal A$-modules. Then for every open
$U\subseteq M$ and every $q>0$,
$$H^q(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0.$$
The Axiom of Choice supplies injective resolutions for module sheaves and for
abelian-sheaf cohomology. Its consequences $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and DC supply,
respectively, the partitions of unity and the acyclic-resolution comparison
used below; no stronger choice principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $I$ be a supplied injective resolution datum on a class $\mathcal D$, let
$F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor, and let
$$0\to A\to J^0\to J^1\to J^2\to\cdots$$
be an $F$-acyclic resolution of $A$ relative to $I$. Assume moreover that
$A\in\mathcal D$ and that, for $Z^0:=A$ and
$$0\to Z^q\to J^q\to Z^{q+1}\to0\qquad(q\ge0),$$
each $Z^q$ lies in $\mathcal D$. Then for every $n\ge 0$ there is a canonical
isomorphism
$$R_I^nF(A)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(F(J^\bullet_{\mathrm{del}})).$$

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

If the filtration on every $C_n$ is finite, the spectral sequence of the filtered chain complex stabilizes pointwise and naturally abuts to $H_n(C)$ with its image filtration. This homology filtration is finite, exhaustive and separated. No uniform filtration bound in n is required.

The **$r$-page** of a filtered complex is the family
$$E^r_{p,q}=Z^r_{p,q}/B^r_{p,q}\quad(r\ge0),$$
with the conventions of [[def-r-cycles-and-r-boundaries-of-an-increasingly-filtered-complex]]. The quotient is licensed by [[lem-r-boundaries-embed-in-r-cycles]]. In particular $E^0_{p,q}=F_pC_{p+q}/F_{p-1}C_{p+q}$.

For $r\ge1$ this is canonically $\bar Z^r_{p,q}/\bar B^r_{p,q}$: the kernel of $A^r_{p,n}\to\operatorname{gr}_pC_n$ is
$$A^r_{p,n}\cap F_{p-1}C_n=A^{r-1}_{p-1,n},$$
since $(p-1)-(r-1)=p-r$. The image of the remaining denominator summand is exactly $\bar B^r$; nested quotients in [[lem-spectral-sequence-subquotient-and-local-lifting-calculus]] give the comparison.

The formula uses only a finite filtration window at each position. More precisely, fix $k\ge0$ and $0\le r\le k$. The filtered complex $F_{p+k}C/F_{p-k-1}C$, with the induced filtration, gives canonically the same $E^r_{p,q}$. Indeed the numerator test uses levels $p,p-r\ge p-k$, and the denominator uses levels $p-1,p+r-1\le p+k$. The removed subcomplex has level $p-k-1$ below every test level, and its contribution in degree $n$ lies in $A^{r-1}_{p-1,n}$ when $r\ge1$, because its differential stays at level $p-k-1\le p-r$. Thus inverse-image tests and the final quotient are unchanged; for $r=0$ this is directly the nested quotient $F_p/F_{p-1}$.

An **abutment to a filtered family** $H_n$ consists of specified isomorphisms
$$E^\infty_{p,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}^F_pH_{p+q}=F_pH_{p+q}/F_{p-1}H_{p+q}.$$
Use [[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]] for the graded pieces, and [[def-limiting-cycles-boundaries-and-e-infinity]] or [[def-spectral-sequence-stabilization-at-a-bidegree]] for the stable terms. On this page every asserted convergence has a finite filtration in each total degree. In particular it is exhaustive and separated. The associated graded family is not identified with the unfiltered target. A morphism of abutments is a filtered map on the $H_n$ whose maps on these quotients agree with the stable-page maps under the specified identifications. For decreasing cohomological filtrations replace the quotient by $F^pH^{p+q}/F^{p+1}H^{p+q}$.

For the pages of a filtered complex there is a specified natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_r:H(E^r,d^r)_{p,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}E^{r+1}_{p,q}\qquad(r\ge0).$$
The homology at $(p,q)$ uses the incoming map from $(p+r,q-r+1)$ and outgoing map to $(p-r,q+r-1)$.

derivations.claim: Suppose $n=0$. Then compactness makes $X$ a finite discrete set of points; there are no forms of positive degree, every Laplacian is zero, and every function is smooth, so the de Rham cohomology is $H^0(X;\mathbb C)=\mathbb C^{\pi_0(X)}$ in degree zero and zero above, the harmonic forms are exactly the locally constant functions, and $H^{0,0}(X)=H^0(X;\mathbb C)$ while $H^{p,q}(X)=0$ otherwise, with the statement's conjugation symmetry, uniqueness and metric-independence vacuous. Here $\Omega_X^0$ is the kernel of $\bar\partial$ on smooth functions, i.e. the sheaf $\underline{\mathbb C}_X$ of locally constant functions, and $H^0(X,\underline{\mathbb C}_X)=\Gamma(X,\underline{\mathbb C}_X)=\mathbb C^{\pi_0(X)}$ with $H^q(X,\underline{\mathbb C}_X)=0$ for $q>0$ because $\underline{\mathbb C}_X$ is a sheaf of modules over the sheaf of smooth functions [F6, F7]; the holomorphic-degree filtration is concentrated in degree zero, so it induces the trivial filtration and the spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ with $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ [F8]. Hence assume $n\ge1$ from now on, so the real dimension of $X$ is $2n\ge2$.

For each degree $k$ let $E$ be the complex Hermitian bundle of complex-valued $k$-forms and $P=\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d$, whose bundles we are given by [F1]. In local coordinates $d$ has leading symbol $i\varepsilon(\xi)$, exterior multiplication by $\xi$, and $d^*$ has leading symbol $-i\lrcorner_\xi$, contraction against $\xi$; since $\varepsilon(\xi)\lrcorner_\xi+\lrcorner_\xi\varepsilon(\xi)=|\xi|^2\mathrm{id}$, the principal symbol of $\Delta_d$ is $\sigma_2(\Delta_d)(x,\xi)=|\xi|^2\mathrm{id}$, a scalar positive-definite quadratic form, so $\Delta_d$ is Laplace type; moreover $\langle\Delta_du,u\rangle=\langle d^*u,d^*u\rangle+\langle du,du\rangle=\|du\|^2+\|d^*u\|^2$ for smooth $u$ by the defining adjoint property of $d^*$ [F1], so the energy is nonnegative, and the same computation read backwards gives $\langle\Delta_du,v\rangle=\langle u,\Delta_dv\rangle$, so $\Delta_d$ is formally symmetric. The bounds and elliptic hypotheses of [F3] are therefore met on the compact boundaryless manifold $X$ of real dimension $2n\ge2$; let $\mathcal H^k=\ker(\Delta_d)$ on $k$-forms, $\Pi_k$ its orthogonal projection and $G_k$ the Green operator. For a smooth $d$-closed $k$-form $u$ one has $u=\Pi_ku+\Delta_dG_ku$; since $\Delta_d$ commutes with $d$ [F2], $\Delta_d(dG_ku)=d(\Delta_dG_ku)=d(u-\Pi_ku)=0$, so $dG_ku$ is harmonic, and it is exact, so $\|dG_ku\|^2=\langle G_ku,d^*(dG_ku)\rangle=0$ because a harmonic form has vanishing adjoint by the energy identity above; hence $dG_ku=0$ and $u=\Pi_ku+dd^*G_ku$. Thus every de Rham class has the smooth harmonic representative $\Pi_ku$, and it is unique: if $h$ is harmonic and $h=d\beta$ for a smooth $\beta$, then $\|h\|^2=\langle\beta,d^*h\rangle=0$, so $h=0$.

By [F2] $\Delta_d=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$ and $\Delta_d$ preserves each bidegree, so $\mathcal H^k=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\mathcal H^{p,q}$ with $\mathcal H^{p,q}=\ker(\Delta_d)\cap\Omega^{p,q}(X)$, an orthogonal sum for the pointwise metric; hence $\Pi_k$ preserves each bidegree. The Green operator $G_k$ does too: if $u$ has pure type, decompose the smooth form $G_ku$ into types. Each component orthogonal to $\mathcal H^k$ solves the corresponding component of $\Delta_dG_ku=u-\Pi_ku$; all other-type components solve the homogeneous equation and are therefore both harmonic and orthogonal to the harmonic space, hence zero. Define $H^{p,q}(X)$ as the image in $H^{p+q}(X;\mathbb C)$ of the $d$-closed forms of type $(p,q)$. A class in $H^{p,q}(X)$ has harmonic representative $\Pi_{p+q}\alpha$ of type $(p,q)$ by bidegree preservation, and conversely a class whose harmonic representative has type $(p,q)$ lies in $H^{p,q}(X)$; since the harmonic representative is unique and additive, $H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X)$ with $H^{p,q}(X)\cong\mathcal H^{p,q}$ via $h\mapsto[h]$. Complex conjugation of complex-valued forms is the conjugate-linear involution induced by the real forms [F1]; it commutes with $d$ and $d^*$, which have real coefficients, hence with $\Delta_d$, and it exchanges $dz_j$ with $d\bar z_j$, hence $\Omega^{p,q}(X)$ with $\Omega^{q,p}(X)$ and $\mathcal H^{p,q}$ with $\mathcal H^{q,p}$; therefore $\overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X)$. Finally $H^{p,q}(X)$ is defined by a closed representative of type $(p,q)$ alone, so it does not depend on the Kähler metric, and the decomposition just proved for one Kähler metric is a decomposition into these metric-free subspaces.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a holomorphic map of compact Kähler manifolds. Pullback of forms is functorial, preserves wedge products and commutes with $d$ [F4], and in holomorphic coordinates $f^*(dz_j)$ and $f^*(d\bar z_j)$ are holomorphic respectively conjugate-holomorphic linear combinations of $dz_k,d\bar z_k$ [F4]; hence $f^*\Omega^{p,q}(Y)\subseteq\Omega^{p,q}(X)$ and $f^*$ carries $d$-closed $(p,q)$-forms to $d$-closed $(p,q)$-forms. Therefore $f^*H^{p,q}(Y)\subseteq H^{p,q}(X)$, so pullback preserves Hodge type; by the naturality in [F4] it is a morphism of the rational structures. For classes $a\in H^{p,q}(X)$, $b\in H^{r,s}(X)$ represented by $d$-closed forms $\alpha,\beta$, the form $\alpha\wedge\beta$ is $d$-closed of type $(p+r,q+s)$ because $d$ is a graded derivation and $\partial,\bar\partial$ have bidegrees $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ [F1], and it represents the cup product $a\smile b$ under the de Rham isomorphism [F4]; hence cup product preserves Hodge type. With $V=H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ finite-dimensional and $V_{\mathbb C}\cong H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ as in [F4], the decomposition $V_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X)$ with conjugation symmetry of step 2.1 and the functoriality just proved make $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ a functorial rational pure Hodge structure in the sense of [F1].

Define the sheaves $\mathcal A^{p,q}$ of smooth $(p,q)$-forms on $X$ and $\Omega_X^p=\ker(\bar\partial:\mathcal A^{p,0}\to\mathcal A^{p,1})$; the sections of $\Omega_X^p$ over an open set are exactly the holomorphic $p$-forms, since $\bar\partial f=0$ is the Cauchy-Riemann condition on the coefficients in degree zero. At each point, the polydisc lemma [F5] provides, for $q\ge1$, a local primitive of every $\bar\partial$-closed $(p,q)$-form on a smaller polydisc, so the stalk sequence $0\to\Omega_X^p\to\mathcal A^{p,0}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\mathcal A^{p,1}\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\mathcal A^{p,n}\to0$ is exact: exactness at $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ holds by the definition of $\Omega_X^p$, and exactness at $\mathcal A^{p,q}$ for $1\le q\le n$ is exactly the local solvability supplied by [F5]. Each $\mathcal A^{p,q}$ is a sheaf of modules over the sheaf of smooth functions (real-valued functions acting by multiplication), and its global sections are the smooth $(p,q)$-forms, so it is acyclic for global sections by [F7], and the acyclic resolution theorem [F7], whose DC hypothesis follows from AC [F7], therefore identifies $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ [F6] with the cohomology of the deleted complex of global sections $\Omega^{p,0}(X)\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\Omega^{p,1}(X)\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots$, i.e. with the global Dolbeault cohomology $H^{p,q}_{\bar\partial}(X)=\ker\bar\partial/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial$ in degree $q$. For a $\bar\partial$-closed smooth $(p,q)$-form $\alpha$ the identity $\alpha=\Pi\alpha+2\Delta_{\bar\partial}G\alpha$ holds because $\Delta_d=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$ [F2]; here $\bar\partial(\Delta_dG\alpha)=\Delta_d(\bar\partial G\alpha)$ by [F2] and equals $\bar\partial(\alpha-\Pi\alpha)=0$, so $\bar\partial G\alpha$ is harmonic, and for any harmonic $v$, $0=\langle\Delta_dv,v\rangle=2(\|\bar\partial v\|^2+\|\bar\partial^*v\|^2)$ by [F2] and adjunction. Thus $\bar\partial^*\bar\partial G\alpha=0$; hence $\alpha=\Pi\alpha+2\bar\partial(\bar\partial^*G\alpha)$ with $\Pi\alpha$ harmonic of type $(p,q)$ by step 2.1, and every Dolbeault class has the harmonic representative $\Pi\alpha$, unique because a harmonic form that is $\bar\partial$-exact has zero norm. Therefore $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)\cong\mathcal H^{p,q}\cong H^{p,q}(X)$ by steps 1.2 and 2.1.

Filter the de Rham complex by holomorphic degree, $F^a\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{r\ge a}\Omega^{r,k-r}(X)$; both $\partial$ and $\bar\partial$ map $F^a$ into $F^a$ by their bidegrees [F1], so the filtration is compatible with $d$ and finite on each degree ($F^a=0$ for $a>k$, $F^a=\Omega^k$ for $a\le0$). Reindex to the homology convention of [F8] by setting $C_m=\Omega^{-m}(X;\mathbb C)$ and the increasing filtration $G_pC_m=F^{-p}\Omega^{-m}(X;\mathbb C)$; [F8] then supplies a spectral sequence with pages $\tilde E^r_{p,q}$ and differentials $\tilde d^r:\tilde E^r_{p,q}\to\tilde E^r_{p-r,q+r-1}$, stabilizing pointwise and abutting to $H_m(C_\bullet)=H^{-m}(X;\mathbb C)$ with the image filtration. Writing $E_r^{a,q}=\tilde E^r_{-a,-q}$ for the cohomological indexing, we get $E_1^{a,q}=H^{a+q}(F^a/F^{a+1})=H^q(\Omega^{a,\bullet},\bar\partial)=H^{a,q}_{\bar\partial}(X)\cong H^{a,q}(X)$ by step 3.2, and $d_r:E_r^{a,q}\to E_r^{a+r,q-r+1}$ is induced by $d$. Each $E_1^{a,q}$ is finite-dimensional by steps 2.1 and 3.2. For a class in $E_1^{a,q}$ represented by the harmonic form $h$ of step 3.2, $dh=\partial h+\bar\partial h=0$ with $\bar\partial h=0$ gives $\partial h=0$, so $d_1=0$. By [F8] each page is naturally the homology of the preceding one, so $E_r$ is a subquotient of $E_1$ and the dimensions are non-increasing in $r$; explicitly $\dim E_{r+1}^{a,q}=\dim E_r^{a,q}-\operatorname{rank}(d_r^{a,q})-\operatorname{rank}(d_r^{a-r,q+r-1})$. The abutment identifies $\operatorname{gr}^aH^k(X;\mathbb C)\cong E_\infty^{a,k-a}$, so $\sum_{a+q=k}\dim E_\infty^{a,q}=\dim H^k(X;\mathbb C)$, while steps 2.1 and 3.2 give $\sum_{a+q=k}\dim E_1^{a,q}=\sum_{a+q=k}\dim H^{a,q}(X)=\dim H^k(X;\mathbb C)$; since $\dim E_\infty^{a,q}\le\dim E_1^{a,q}$ for every $(a,q)$, the diagonal sums being equal forces $\dim E_\infty^{a,q}=\dim E_1^{a,q}$ termwise, hence every rank vanishes and $d_r=0$ for all $r\ge1$ with $E_\infty=E_1$, whence $\operatorname{gr}^aH^k(X;\mathbb C)\cong H^{a,k-a}(X)$ and the spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ with $E_1^{a,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^a)$. Finally the image filtration is $F^aH^k(X;\mathbb C)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^k(F^a\Omega^\bullet)\to H^k(X;\mathbb C)\bigr)$ [F8], which is the set of classes with a $d$-closed representative in $\bigoplus_{r\ge a}\Omega^{r,k-r}(X)$; it contains $\bigoplus_{r\ge a}H^{r,k-r}(X)$ because such a class has a closed representative of pure type, and its successive graded quotients are $\operatorname{gr}^rH^k\cong H^{r,k-r}(X)$, so the finite filtrations have equal dimensions and $F^aH^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{r\ge a}H^{r,k-r}(X)$, as asserted.

Throughout this page, assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]): the
analytic and cohomological suppliers invoked by the results below assume full
AC, and each item records its exact use. The definitional content below uses no
choice.

**(1) Compact Kähler manifolds.** Let $n\ge1$. A **Kähler manifold** is a complex
manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with complex structure
$J$ and a **Hermitian metric** $g$ — a Riemannian metric
([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) satisfying
$g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$ for all tangent vectors $v,w$ — whose **real fundamental form**
$\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ is

- a smooth real 2-form, the section of $\Lambda^2T^*X$ obtained by alternating
  $g(J\cdot,\cdot)$;
- **positive**: $\omega(v,Jv)=g(Jv,Jv)>0$ for every nonzero tangent vector $v$;
- **closed**: $d\omega=0$.

The manifold is **compact Kähler** when the topological space $X$ is compact.

**Orientation.** For a complex basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ of a tangent space $T_xX$,
the ordered real basis $(v_1,Jv_1,\dots,v_n,Jv_n)$ is declared **positive**. This
is well defined: two complex bases differ by a complex-linear automorphism, whose
real determinant is the square of the modulus of its complex determinant and so
is positive, and the local orientations therefore glue along holomorphic charts
to a global orientation of $X$. Let $v_1,\dots,v_n$ be a $g$-orthonormal complex
frame, so $g(v_j,v_k)=\delta_{jk}$ and $g(v_j,Jv_k)=0$, and let $e_j=g(v_j,\cdot)$ and
$f_j=g(Jv_j,\cdot)$ be the metric-dual covectors. Then
$(e_1,f_1,\dots,e_n,f_n)$ is a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe,
$f_j=-Je_j$ for the pullback action $(J\alpha)(v)=\alpha(Jv)$ of $J$ on
covectors, and

$$\omega=\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\wedge f_j .$$

The **oriented volume form** is the top form

$$dV:=\frac{\omega^n}{n!}=e_1\wedge f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n\wedge f_n ,$$

which evaluates to $1$ on each positively oriented $g$-orthonormal frame.

**Complex dimension zero.** For $n=0$ a complex manifold is a discrete space and
compactness makes it a finite set of points with its unique complex structure;
there are no tangent vectors and no forms of positive degree, $\omega=0$, and the
operators $L,\Lambda,\partial,\bar\partial,d,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ and
all Laplacians introduced below are zero. The Hodge star is the identity on
degree zero, and $dV$ is the counting measure.

**(2) Complex-valued forms and Kähler operators.** Let $X$ be compact Kähler.
Write $\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ for the complex-valued smooth $k$-forms, the
complex-linear extension of the real forms of
[[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]; the Hodge star $*$ of
[[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] extends complex-linearly, and for
$\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)$ the **integral inner product**

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\int_X\alpha\wedge*\bar\beta$$

is complex-linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second; the
integral is that of
[[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]] and
the integrand is $\lvert\alpha\rvert^2\,dV$ when $\beta=\alpha$, so the pairing
is a positive definite Hermitian form. In holomorphic charts

$$\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(X),\qquad d=\partial+\bar\partial ,$$

with $\partial$ and $\bar\partial$ of bidegree $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$
([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]]); the decomposition is independent
of the holomorphic chart because holomorphic chart changes preserve bidegree.

Put $L=\omega\wedge$, so that $L:\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)\to\Omega^{k+2}(X;\mathbb C)$,
and let $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ be the formal adjoints of
$L,\partial,\bar\partial,d$ with respect to $\langle\,,\rangle$; existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]], applied
to the bundle of complex-valued forms with the metric of
[[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]
and the density $dV$. The **Laplacians** are

$$\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d,\qquad \Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial,\qquad \Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial ,$$

and $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

**(3) Rational pure Hodge structures.** Let $k\in\mathbb Z$. A **rational pure
Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space
$V$ together with a direct-sum decomposition by $\mathbb C$-subspaces

$$V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q},\qquad \overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p},$$

where conjugation is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear involution
$v\otimes\lambda\mapsto v\otimes\bar\lambda$. The sum is finite because
$V_{\mathbb C}$ is finite dimensional, and it is direct by definition. The **Weil
operator** $C$ is the $\mathbb C$-linear endomorphism of $V_{\mathbb C}$ acting
as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$; the conjugation symmetry makes $C$ commute with
conjugation, so $C$ is the complexification of a real-linear endomorphism
of $V_{\mathbb R}=V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb R$. It need not preserve $V$.

A **polarization** of such a Hodge structure is a nondegenerate $\mathbb Q$-bilinear
form $Q:V\times V\to\mathbb Q$, extended $\mathbb C$-bilinearly to $V_{\mathbb C}$,
such that

- $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$ for all $x,y$;
- $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$;
- $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ is a positive definite Hermitian form on $V_{\mathbb C}$.

A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace
$U\subseteq V$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$.
The **Tate shift** $V(-r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, keeps the underlying $\mathbb Q$-vector
space, the Weil operator and $Q$ as they are and moves the bidegrees to
$(p+r,q+r)$, so that the weight becomes $k+2r$; equivalently, $(V(-r))^{p,q}=V^{p-r,q-r}$.

Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de
Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and
$$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$
Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth
representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the
Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the
kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms),
$H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration
$F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration
induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose
spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$.
Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product
preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge
structure.

Assume AC. For a compact smooth manifold $X$, the natural coefficient maps
induce isomorphisms $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}F\cong H^k(X;F)$ for
every characteristic-zero field $F$, finite-dimensional in each degree. For
$F=\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ these identify singular cohomology with the real or
complex de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps
between such manifolds. No ordered-field or positivity structure is asserted
for a general $F$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
